name: Kom
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 5 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Shultz, George. 1997. Kom Language Grammar Sketch, Part 1. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research (Republic of Cameroon). 41 pp. (open PDF, sil.org via archived copy (Internet Archive, 2023))
catalog_quote: Kom is a tonal language. There are three level tones (high, mid, low) and three primary contour tones (low-falling, high-low, high-mid). Other contour tones rarely occur as a result of tone modification within the phrase. Only low and high-low tones are marked in the orthography. Vowel lengthening occasionally occurs in conjunction with a high-low tone or an emphatic utterance. This is not marked separately from the high-low tone mark. Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.citation: Shultz, George. 1997. Kom Language Grammar Sketch, Part 1. Yaoundé: SIL / Ministry of Scientific and Technical Research (Republic of Cameroon). 41 pp.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (42 pp. footer "G. Shultz, SIL.. page 5 of 41" on PDF page 6). The text is codepoint-shifted by +1 (raw: "Rsqdrr hr gd`qc nmkx hm dlog`shb roddbg ats hr mns l`qjdc-"); I decoded it independently and also rendered PDF page 6 to PNG (110 dpi) and read the image. §2.2 "Suprasegmental phonemes" reads exactly as quoted, all seven sentences, ending "Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked." Verbatim confirmed at the stated locator (§2.2, printed p. 5 = p. 6). Reading: Kom is described as a three-level-tone language (H, M, L; contours low-falling, high-low, high-mid) with tone modification within the phrase; the only stress remark is that stress is heard only in emphatic s…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kom is a three-level-tone language (H, M, L plus contour tones) with lexical and grammatical tone; there is no lexical or positional word stress. Perceptible stress occurs only as a feature of emphatic speech and is not. No position for stress is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the only qualification is that stress (and vowel lengthening) can be heard in emphatic utterances.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the language in general (suprasegmental phonemes); stress is tied to emphatic utterances, i.e. a pragmatic/phrase-level phenomenon, not the phonological word. Corroborated by Shultz 1993 (phonology notes, 23 pp.), Hyman 1984 (tonology ms., 95 sheets) and Kawuldim 2008 (§1.5), none of which mentions stress at all.
new_statements.identity_note: Shultz 1997 describes the main Kom dialect (Itaŋikom), which he says serves 95% of speakers; Mbesa and Ake village varieties are noted as closely related. All sources are for Kom of Boyo Division, Northwest Cameroon = komc1235 [bkm]; Bruens's 'Nkom' is the same language under an older name.

As an extra spot-check I a full-text search for stress/accent the other on-disk Kom sources in the folder (Hyman 1984 Kom Tonology scanned, Chia & Kimbi 1992 alphabet guide scanned, Kawuldim 2008 thesis text, Shultz 1997 decoded text) for stress|accent|prominen|emphat: the only hits are Shultz 1997 §2.2 p. 5 ('Stress is heard only in emphatic speech but is not marked.'), which is already the catalog's existing statement, and unrelated 'emphatic subject/particle' glosses in Kawuldim. Nothing missed.

tone_statements.citation: Faytak, Matthew, Tianle Yang & Ivo Forghema Njuasi. 2026. Acoustic correlates of positional prominence in Kom. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2026, 392-396. ISCA. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2026-79
tone_statements.quote: This study investigates phonetic cues to positional prominence in the vowels of Kom, a Grassfields Bantu language of Cameroon with lexical tone. Many tone languages have been reported either to lack some or all of the usual phonetic correlates of word prominence or to lack stress altogether. [...] Findings suggest that vowels in prominent positions have differences in formant values and duration consistent with hyperarticulation relative to non-prominent positions. The presence of at least some cues to prominence in Kom underscores the need to further investigate the (non)existence of stress in African tone languages.

tone_statements.quote: (9) A language may have both HTS and LTS [...] b. /nè fé-ghàm -fé/ [nè fè-ghām̀-fè˚] 'with a mat' (Kom; *LH) [...] (iii) Many languages which have both HTS and LTS restrict LTS in ways they do not restrict HTS. In Kuki-Thaadow, LTS will not apply to a /L-H-H/ input, but HTS will apply to /H-L-L/. tone_statements.summary: Kom: underlying /H, L/ with floating tones; H spreads onto following L (creating M/HL surface contours), L spreads onto following H except before a floating L; no prepausal LH rise; level L˚ before pause.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Same language as the catalog (Kom, SIL Cameroon field research June 1989 to March 1991, research assistant Pius Loh). The work says nothing on stress; its three-level-plus-contour tone description is fully compatible with the existing statement from Shultz 1997 §2.2 ("Kom is a tonal language.. sources.citation: Shultz, George. 1993 (June). Notes on the Phonology of the Kom Language. Yaoundé: SIL Cameroon. 22 pp.
sources.note: Whole paper is phonology (23-page scan, scanned). §8 Tone (pp. 14-15): eight phonetic pitches, three level (H, M, L) and five contour; lexical and grammatical tone; downstep. §4 Word structure: words of 1-4 syllables, monosyllables most frequent. sources.locator: abstract (ISCA Archive landing page; paper pp. 392-396)
sources.note: States Kom has lexical tone and is a word-PROSODY study: acoustic cues (duration, F1/F2) to stem-initial positional prominence; full vowel inventory only in stem-initial syllables, /i a ɨ/ elsewhere; finds hyperarticulation cues in prominent position and argues the (non)existence of stress in African tone languages needs re-examination. Directly bears on the catalog's 'no word stress' line for Kom (Shultz 1997). Body (tone background section, tone control in the stats) unseen.
